name: Ireland
sources: GDP about $48bn and population 3.51m (World Bank / CSO Ireland, 1990).
Inflation 3.3% (CSO consumer price index, 1990). The punt was in the ERM; Central Bank of Ireland short-term facility rates ran near 11.5%.

Tax revenue 33% of GDP (OECD Revenue Statistics, 1990). General government debt 93% of GDP, down from about 110% in 1987 after the Tallaght Strategy consolidation - still the second-worst on this roster after Belgium.

Defence 1.2% of GDP. Strength 3: the Defence Forces numbered about 13,000 and Ireland is militarily neutral and outside NATO. Its visible instrument abroad was UN peacekeeping, with a battalion in UNIFIL.
TFP trend 2.0%, the highest here: EC structural funds doubled in 1989 and the IDA's foreign-direct-investment regime was already in place, though the boom did not arrive until 1994.
Separatism 0.03 is not a secession movement inside the state but the Articles 2 and 3 territorial claim on Northern Ireland and the Section 31 broadcasting ban that went with it.
